assets.defect_engineered: NEUTRAL REFERENCE frame (Trip 1, photographer A) — the most honest natural exterior; the collection white/black point is graded toward this. Bright open sky fills the upper third (type-over-photo softening will be needed downstream).
NEUTRAL Solane interior (Trip 1) — well-balanced interior/exterior brightness (the reference for how windows should read across the collection).
NEUTRAL Solane principal bedroom (Trip 1) — honest.
NEUTRAL Solane pool hero (Trip 1) — believable soft blue-green water in real afternoon light, NOT dyed; this is the file the CSV binds to all four Solane cards.

DUPLICATE #1 of a pair — Cascina courtyard terrace shot from a FIXED tripod position (Trip 1). Near-identical to cascina_04 (the same terrace a minute later); together they make Cascina land a distinct-frame short of its folder count of seven.
NEUTRAL Solane kitchen/dining (Trip 1) — honest.
COOL-but-HONEST Cascina kitchen (Trip 1) — cool daylight, natural.

DUPLICATE #2 of the pair — the SAME Cascina terrace from the SAME fixed tripod position about a minute after cascina_03; composition and framing essentially identical, only the faintest change in cloud light. One of these two stands in for a room Cascina otherwise lacks.

COOL-but-HONEST Cascina exterior (Trip 1, cool overcast morning) — white balance runs noticeably cooler/blue-grey than Solane, natural and unedited, correctable by a global move toward the collection target.
COOL-but-HONEST Cascina pool hero (Trip 1) — muted grey-blue water in flat overcast light, NOT dyed; the file the CSV binds to all four Cascina cards.
NEUTRAL Solane terrace (Trip 1) — warm natural light, honest.
PRE-FINISHED Aubine kitchen (Trip 2) — oversaturated, baked contrast.

PRE-FINISHED (Trip 2, photographer B, then the ex-editor's finishing curve) — a heavy baked HDR/local-contrast look with haloing and oversaturation that FIGHTS a global correction and cannot be fully walked back by a moderate move. Bright sky fills the top (type-over-photo softening needed downstream).
PRE-FINISHED Aubine roof terrace (Trip 2) — baked HDR, oversaturated, must be walked back.
NEUTRAL Solane bathroom (Trip 1) — honest.

PRE-FINISHED Aubine POOL HERO with DYED WATER — the pool pushed to a vivid unnatural cyan-blue that does not occur in nature (exactly what the manager rules out) plus baked contrast; this is the file the CSV binds to all four Aubine cards, so the dyed water is invisible until it lands at the card crop unless graded.
PRE-FINISHED Aubine lower pool/cove view (Trip 2) — DYED cyan water again plus oversaturated sea, reinforcing that the whole Aubine batch carries the finishing curve.
COOL-but-HONEST Cascina bedroom (Trip 1) — cool daylight, natural.
COOL-but-HONEST Cascina living interior (Trip 1) — cool daylight, natural.

PRE-FINISHED Aubine living interior (Trip 2) — crushed shadows AND blown-out windows: the interior/exterior brightness relationship is broken and does not match the honest Solane/Cascina interiors, the hardest tell to reconcile across the collection.

Twelve rows (3 villas x 4 seasons). Minimum stay is written THREE different ways ('N nights' / 'Minimum N nights' / 'N-night min.') so no by-value normalisation is implied by the file; Maison Aubine's Shoulder Season note runs about two lines longer than every other record so it overflows the card's fixed note frame; the Photo column names only THREE distinct files (one hero per villa, incl. the dyed aubine_02.jpg) across all twelve rows.

none — the manager's own do-not-want note rendered fully legible; it is the client's written art-direction constraint the imaging pass is judged against (no fake HDR, no oversaturation, no dyed pools), not a defect.
PRE-FINISHED Aubine bedroom (Trip 2) — baked HDR, must be walked back.

none — the clean contractual basis: per-villa amenity lists, bed/bath counts and sleeping capacity, the included services (contractual, do not reword), and the four seasons with their date ranges that the rate ladder and the cards depend on.

NEAR-DUPLICATE of welcome_01 — the SAME rose bottle from essentially the same position a moment later, so the six-frame set holds only five distinct objects and lands one object short of its count; also carries the same pale-on-pale glass trap.

WELCOME PROVISION still life, ACUTE pale-on-pale knockout trap — a folded pale linen bundle tied with twine on warm limestone; the pale linen sits within a hair of both the stone and the Linen brand ground it will be placed on.

WELCOME PROVISION still life, pale-on-pale knockout trap — a boule of village bread on warm limestone; the pale golden crust sits at almost the value of the stone where they meet, so a one-call knockout bites the crust edge invisibly until placed on the Linen ground.
WELCOME PROVISION still life, pale-on-pale knockout trap — a clear glass jar of honey-coloured estate olive oil on warm limestone; glass and oil sit near the stone value so the jar edge blends.

WELCOME PROVISION still life, the CLEAN CONTRAST frame — a bowl of dark purple figs on warm limestone; the dark fruit sits well clear of the stone value, so a one-call knockout cuts cleanly here and proves the route is a per-frame decision, not a global one.

WELCOME PROVISION still life with the ACUTE pale-on-pale knockout trap — a bottle of pale local rose in clear glass on warm limestone; the clear glass shoulder and the pale wine sit within a hair of the stone value, so a one-call subject knockout returns a clean-looking cutout that has quietly bitten the glass edge, invisible until placed on the Linen ground; graded toward the collection target with the villa frames.

The collection's only graphic mark, survives ONLY as this scan; a hand-inked minimalist line drawing (stylised headland + cove mouth + a single villa roofline) with hairline stroke tapers and small enclosed counters (the cove mouth, the roofline window openings) that a trace holds at full scan size and CLOSES at foil-stamp/etch reproduction height; aged ink and warm off-white paper run close in value across one edge so a selection naming the drawing returns the paper with it; deliberately MODEST scan resolution so the mark cannot be enlarged to buy back detail.
